LC_COMMON_kvk_historyrank_rule1:
1. For each Biozone event, the top zone receives a gold medal. The second-place zone receives a silver medal, and the third-place zone receives a bronze medal.
2. Zone ranking is based on the number of gold medals each zone has. When the number of gold medals is the same, ranking will be based on the number of silver medals. When the number of silver medals is the same, ranking will be based on the number of bronze medals.
3. Zones with no medals will not enter the leaderboard.
LC_COMMON_kvk_historyrank_rule2:
1. For each Biozone event, the top Commander receives a gold medal. The second to 10th place Commanders receive a silver medal. The 11th to 50th place Commanders receive a bronze medal.
2. Individual ranking is based on the number of gold medals each Commander has. When the number of gold medals is the same, ranking will be based on the number of silver medals. When the number of silver medals is the same, ranking will be based on the number of bronze medals.
3. Commanders with no medals will not enter the leaderboard.

LC_COMMON_kvk_warzone_bounty_rule:
The enemy is concerned by the counterattacks on Biozone from various Zones. They've decided to put a bounty on the most powerful of these Zones, with the hope of pitting Commanders from different areas against one another.
1. At the start of each event, based on the overall situation of each War Zone, Dr. Pandora will collect information and designate one War Zone as the “Target Zone” for this round, issuing a high-value bounty.
2. If players from the other three Zones successfully prevent the "Target Zone" from reaching number 1 on the Honor Leaderboard, then they will share the bounty rewards placed on that target.
3. The final bounty reward each player receives is dependent on the Honor Points they earn during the event. The higher the points, the higher the bounty earned.

LC_COMMON_monopoly_rules:
1. You earn event items by taking part in the event or buying event packs.
2. Each throw costs a certain amount of event items.
3. You earn rewards for the tiles you land on.
4. Walking onto an Event tile triggers a random event.
5. Make it to the goal to complete a lap.
6. You earn lap rewards for every lap you complete.
7. Complete a certain number of laps to earn extra rewards.
8. Unused event items will be removed once the event ends. 
9. If you tick in 'Skip animation', pips selections will instead be randomized
10. You get 1 point for each throw and 10 for each completed lap. You will be ranked based on your points, with rank rewards being sent to your mailbox after the event.

2. Conquest Points can be exchanged for items in the Zone Store.
3. The Zone Store's stock will improve as the counter offense advances.
4. Conquest Points are reset at the end of the season, so be sure to use them before that!

LC_COMMON_return_dead_troops_text1: The wreckage of tanks and tank destroyers will not be left to corrode on the battlefield—special troops will collect them and return them to working condition so that their sturdy armor will continue to make contributions to the war effort.
LC_COMMON_return_dead_troops_help:
A certain proportion of units lost in the Biozone will be returned when the Biozone ends.
1. Only units lost in the Biozone will be returned.
2. Only after the Biozone ends will the losses be tallied and the units returned.
3. You will get a base return percentage when you enter the Biozone; this percentage can be increased by completing events, up to a max of 60%.
4.Unused [Wrench] will be reclaimed at the end of the event.

LC_COMMON_Lucky_Discount_rules_d:
1. The Fortune Discount event restarts on the 25th of each month.
 2. Some of the War Zone Market's base decorations and officer outfits become part of the Fortune Discount's prize pool at that time. Tap the reward pool to see what items it contains for the current month.
 3. You can draw new discounted decorations and outfits in each Fortune Discount event.
 4. Only the highest possible discount tier is shown in the prize pool, and draws you make might be with a lower discount.
 5. Decorations and outfits that's been in the prize pool for longer have a higher chance of appearing with a high discount.
 6. You cannot draw decorations and outfits you already own from the prize pool.
 7. You cannot draw from the prize pool if you already own all the rewards it contains, but you'll be able to claim a gift on that month instead.
 8. Decoration and outfit discounts won't be retained if you switch servers, and you'll have to draw discounts anew.

LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_01_desc: The 14-inch Single-Barrel Cannon of the Japanese Navy, widely used on Japan's main forces ships and light cruisers after World War I.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_02_desc: Officially named the 12.7cm SK C/34, it is the standard main gun for most German Navy destroyers.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_03_desc: The American 5-inch/38-caliber MK12, is one of the most outstanding dual-purpose high-altitude and flat-trajectory guns in World War II.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_04_desc: The Soviet 130 mm/50 B13 Pattern 1936, was widely used during World War II.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_05_desc: Officially named the 12.7 cm/50 Type 3, it is the naval gun mounted on small vessels of the former Imperial Japanese Navy.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_06_desc: Twin version of the American 5-inch/38-caliber MK12.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_07_desc: The German 15cm/55 SK C/28 twin version, commonly used as secondary armament on warships.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_08_desc: The British 5.25"/50 QF Mark I cannon is used as a dual-purpose secondary gun on the King George V-class battleships, and as the main gun on the Dido-class light cruisers.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_09_desc: Originally designated as the 120 mm/50 Model 1926, it was developed by the Ansaldo company in 1926. Subsequently, several derivative models were developed.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_10_desc: The first large-caliber artillery piece entirely designed, developed, and manufactured by Japan.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_11_desc: Based on the B-13's 130mm twin cannon, the naval turret has relatively weak anti-aircraft capabilities.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_12_desc: The German 38 cm SK C/34 twin cannon, is the main gun of the famous Bismarck-class.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_13_desc: The American 6 inch/47 Mk.16 (152 mm), is the main gun of the Brooklyn and Cleveland-class.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_14_desc: The British 16 inch/45 (40.6 cm) Mark I, the main gun of the Nelson-class battleships, was once the most powerful naval main gun in the world at the beginning of its service.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_15_desc: The American 8 inch/55 (20.3 cm) Mark 9, this gun was used on American treaty cruisers and Lexington-class aircraft carriers.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_16_desc: The M1909 Triple Main Gun of Italy is one of the earliest triple main guns on battleships in the world.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_17_desc: The German 28 cm/52 SK C/28 triple cannon, is the main gun of the Deutschland-class armored ships.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_18_desc: The German 15 cm/60 SK C/25 triple cannon, primarily used on light cruisers.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_19_desc: The main cannon of the Japanese Yamato-class battleship is the largest caliber battleship main cannon in history.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_20_desc: The Mk 6 cannon demonstrated its formidable power multiple times throughout the history of the United States Navy in World War II.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_21_desc: The 380 mm/45 Model 1935 cannon is the last type of battleship main gun developed by France, boasting impressive power.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_22_desc: Made in the Soviet Union, each turret is equipped with a radar rangefinder.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_23_desc: Lighter than the Mark 9, with stronger firepower.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_24_desc: Developed based on the old version from WWII, it has seen improvements in both firing rate and anti-aircraft capabilities.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_25_desc: A product of the Soviet designers' wild experiments, it was never deployed in actual combat. With a total weight of about 10 tons, it could fire shells weighing 250~300 kilograms to a distance of 13,730 meters.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_26_desc: Made in Germany. The largest caliber naval artillery in history, but it was never used in actual combat.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_27_desc: The main cannon of the Soviet-class battleship, possessing an ultra-long range and strong penetration power. However, due to the influence of ammunition, it did not achieve the expected effect.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_28_desc: With a total weight of 11.2000 tons, it is the first French triple 152mm turret.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_01_desc: The M2 Browning is widely used in various combat scenarios and is one of the most famous and successful machine guns of the 20th century.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_02_desc: The Oerlikon 20 mm Gun, which was equipped by the United States Navy starting in '41, is a very effective short-range anti-aircraft weapon.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_03_desc: Officially named the 3.7cm SK C/30, it boasts powerful firepower, but its rate of fire is its shortcoming.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_04_desc: The Type 96 25 mm AA gun was widely used on various types of ships in the former Japanese Navy. Its drawbacks include insufficient firing rate and power, and a lack of fire control.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_05_desc: Twin-mounted Oerlikon 20 mm Gun, providing more concentrated firepower.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_06_desc: Officially named the 12.7 cm/40 Type 89 naval gun, it is the most representative anti-aircraft gun of Japan.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_07_desc: The 4 inch/45 QF Mark V was initially used as a main gun, later it was used by the British Navy as a long-range anti-aircraft weapon.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_08_desc: Officially named the 37 mm/67 70-K, it features rapid firing, reliability, and adaptability, playing a significant role in the anti-aircraft operations of the Soviet Union and its allies.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_09_desc: Officially named the QF 2-pounder, it is more commonly referred to as the Pom-Pom, a name derived from the sound it makes when firing.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_10_desc: The Twin-mounted Type 96 25 mm AA gun fires alternately from the left and right. While one side ceases fire to replace the ammunition magazine and prepare for the next round, the other continues to fire, thus maintaining uninterrupted continuous shooting.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_11_desc: The American 1.1 inch/75 Mark 1, in pursuit of the ultimate firing speed, resulted in poor stability.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_12_desc: The 40mm L60 Bofors, was the most successful mid-range anti-aircraft weapon during World War II, and was equipped by various countries.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_13_desc: Quad-mounted 40mm L60 Bofors, with a higher density of firepower, is a very effective anti-aircraft weapon when combined with the fire control system.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_14_desc: The British QF 2-pounder Mk VIII gun, this weapon was redesigned from the QF 2-pounder Mk II to adapt to the octuple turret.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_15_desc: Quad-mounted 2cm Flakvierling C/38, with a high density of firepower, is the main short-range anti-aircraft weapon of Germany, but its power is limited and its range is relatively short.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_16_desc: The American 3 inch/50 Mark 33, appeared towards the end of World War II and continued to serve on most warships until the Cold War period.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_17_desc: In response to the issue of insufficient range and power of the 40mm anti-aircraft gun that emerged towards the end of the war, Bofors company increased the caliber based on it and developed a 57mm anti-aircraft gun, which greatly improved both the destructive power and range.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_18_desc: Triple-mounted Type 96 25 mm AA gun, possessing ultimate firing rate and concentrated firepower.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_19_desc: The Storm Shield variant of the triple-mounted Type 96 25 mm AA gun, equipped exclusively on the Yamato-class battleships. It has a more robust structure and higher strength.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_20_desc: The automatic rapid-fire cannon for short-range air defense, born in the Soviet Union in the 70s, is highly innovative and advanced.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_21_desc: Weighing 21 tons, it is equipped with six Bofors guns in pursuit of firepower, and can be linked with the fire control system.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_22_desc: This type of anti-aircraft gun adopted a layout with independent sights and weapons, and was highly automated, which was a quite advanced design in the 1930s.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_23_desc: The anti-aircraft gun was developed by the Soviet Union to address its weak air defense issue. In order to enhance performance and power, it used a 45 mm caliber and adopted a chain feed for ammunition, making it an outstanding anti-aircraft gun at the time.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_24_desc: Utilizes optical tracking/radio command guidance, excels at striking low-altitude sea-skimming aircraft, with high reliability.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_25_desc: An automatic twin-barrel anti-aircraft gun with radar fire control, with a firing rate of up to 1000 rounds/min.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_26_desc: The Seaslug is the first generation of anti-aircraft missiles of the Royal Navy of the United Kingdom, with a very unique shape, equipped with four circumferential booster engines at the warhead position.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_27_desc: The Mk-13 GMLS is a single-arm missile launcher capable of launching various missiles. Due to its unique single-arm design, it is often referred to as the "One-Armed Bandit".
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_28_desc: The OSA-M is a short-range anti-air missile system developed by Russia, used to intercept low-altitude flying targets, and possesses high speed, maneuverability, and infrared guidance capabilities.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_01_desc: Early anti-submarine weapons, deepwater bombs could be projected to distant locations through a projector. Commonly known as the K-GUN.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_02_desc: The prototype is the Russian BMB-1 Deepwater Bomb Launcher, widely equipped on Soviet destroyers during World War II.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_03_desc: The 610mm torpedo first appeared on Japanese warships.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_04_desc: The 550mm torpedo first appeared on French warships.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_05_desc: The prototype is the Japanese Type 94 Depth Charge Projector, and the United States also developed a similarly styled projector, commonly known as the Y-GUN.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_06_desc: French triple 550mm torpedo launcher, by using a speed reduction plugin, it can also launch torpedoes of 533mm and 450mm caliber.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_07_desc: The 610mm torpedo in triple mount, officially named as Type 12 Triple Torpedo Tube 610mm.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_08_desc: 533mm is the mainstream torpedo caliber in navies around the world, and triple launchers are commonly found on destroyers and light cruisers.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_09_desc: Commonly found on destroyers, such as the Fletcher-class from the United States.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_10_desc: A type of test torpedo developed by the French Navy at the end of the war, which added oxygen propulsion to the original 550mm torpedo.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_11_desc: Torpedo launchers commonly found on Japanese destroyers are also used on various heavy cruisers.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_12_desc: The Italian W270 Torpedo, with a specially tapered head structure, facilitates increased cruising speed.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_13_desc: This torpedo launcher is a hexa-mount, which is more powerful than the commonly seen quad-mount.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_14_desc: The Soviet RBU-1000 model with a 6-tube launcher can fire 305mm RGB-10 anti-submarine rockets. In addition to conventional anti-submarine warfare, it can also be used to intercept torpedoes.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_15_desc: The MK32 Triple Torpedo Launcher is a common anti-submarine weapon, and due to its convenient arrangement, this type of equipment can be seen on various warships.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_16_desc: The British invented an anti-submarine weapon based on the principle of a mortar, known as the Squid.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_17_desc: Often referred to as the "Mousetrap", it uses rocket propulsion for launching, thus it does not produce recoil, greatly reducing the pressure on the ship's deck.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_18_desc: The BMB-2 is a type of Soviet deepwater bomb launcher with a caliber of 433mm. Compared to the rolling projection method, this type of projection covers a larger area.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_19_desc: A forward-firing anti-submarine weapon developed by the United Kingdom, based on the principle of a spigot mortar, capable of firing a total of 24 rounds. The name "Hedgehog" comes from its appearance.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_20_desc: Primarily equipped with the SET-53 series of anti-submarine torpedoes, it can also launch heavy anti-ship torpedoes of the same caliber. Installed on the Type 1135 frigate.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_21_desc: The Alpha Anti-Submarine Weapon is a type of rocket depth charge launcher. This weapon resembles an artillery piece, but its ammunition is a rocket depth charge (RUR-4).
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_22_desc: The Limbo Depth Charge Projector, also known as the "A/S Mk.10" Depth Charge Gun, is an improvement from the "Squid" Depth Charge Gun. It has been widely used in the Royal Navy of the United Kingdom, the Australian Navy, and the Canadian Navy.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_23_desc: The German G7 series torpedoes, the lowercase letters at the end indicate the propulsion method, 'a' for steam, 'e' for electric, and 'u' for hydrogen peroxide. The G7a is used for destroyers and submarines with a caliber of 533mm.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_24_desc: The Smerch-1 is an anti-submarine equipment from the early Cold War period in the Soviet Union. After learning from the experience of the "Mousetrap", it improved the issues of fixed elevation angle and lack of directional aiming structure.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_25_desc: The RUR-5 ASROC (Anti-Submarine Rocket) is launched using the MK-112 "Matchbox" Launcher, a type of all-weather, all-sea-state anti-submarine missile system. It is widely used on various warships of the United States Navy.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_26_desc: Quad-mounted M/50 Anti-Submarine Rocket Launcher, developed by the Swedish Bofors company in 1950. In the 1950s, when the performance of anti-submarine torpedoes was not good, anti-submarine rockets were considered to be good close-range anti-submarine weapons.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_27_desc: Malafon (MArine LAtécoère FONds) is an anti-submarine missile system developed by France, used for surface vessels to precisely strike and track submarine targets in anti-submarine warfare.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_28_desc: The RPK-3 Metel is a series of Soviet anti-submarine and anti-ship missile systems, developed in the 1960s and deployed on numerous vessels.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_01_desc: The earliest anti-air radar appeared in the late 1930s, this radar, which uses a spring bed-style antenna, can provide air warning functions.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_02_desc: The antenna of the maritime radar is smaller than that of the anti-air radar, allowing it to be installed in more locations. It provides maritime search capabilities.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_03_desc: This basic passive sonar is a common anti-submarine search device found on various warships.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_04_desc: Heat-treated homogeneous armor, shells entering at a large angle will ricochet when they encounter horizontal armor made of homogeneous armor steel.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_05_desc: Enhanced Passive Sonar with Improved Accuracy.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_06_desc: The prototype is the American CXAM radar, which performs excellently and can achieve air warning at a distance of about 100KM.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_07_desc: The prototype is the British Type 271 Radar, which has modified transmitting and receiving antennas, and is equipped with a PPI display.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_08_desc: Carburized Surface Hardened Armor can effectively resist armor-piercing bullets and is often used in the armor belts of large warships.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_09_desc: Radar used to detect targets and guide weapon launches using electromagnetic waves.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_10_desc: Utilizes more advanced sensor materials, further increasing accuracy and reducing noise.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_11_desc: The American SK series anti-air radar is the second generation of air search radar, equipped with a PPI display, greatly facilitating operation.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_12_desc: The first American surface search radar with a wavelength of 10 centimeters, in addition to maritime search, it can also detect low-altitude aircraft.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_13_desc: The American Mark 4 (FD) Fire-Control Radar, along with the first Mk 37 Naval Artillery Fire-Control System, is one of the best dual-purpose high-altitude and flat-trajectory fire-control systems during the war.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_14_desc: Wireless communication greatly improves the efficiency of information dissemination, providing timely instructions, intelligence, and support for military operations.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_15_desc: The Yarrow boiler used by the Queen Elizabeth-class battleships is a more efficient new type of boiler, which once caused a revolution in the power system.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_16_desc: Unlike steam turbines and boilers, the diesel engine is an internal combustion engine. Diesel engines have lower fuel consumption, making them particularly suitable for warships that require long range.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_17_desc: SO-Type Radar, characterized by its small size and light weight, is suitable for installation on small vessels.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_18_desc: The SK-2 Radar is an improvement on the SK Radar, it is a Large Long-Wave Anti-Air Radar, mainly equipped on large military vessels.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_19_desc: The Mk-8 Fire-Control Radar, composed of 42 rod-shaped antennas, can be used in all weather conditions. It is mainly used for battleships and other large military vessels.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_20_desc: The Pugliese system, designed by Navy Lieutenant Colonel Umberto Pugliese in early 1917, is a form of "energy-absorbing" protection specifically designed to offset the damage to the underwater hull caused by the explosion of torpedoes or mines.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_21_desc: This is the fire-control radar for the dual-purpose high-altitude artillery, responsible for directing secondary artillery fire and air defense.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_22_desc: The DRBC (Détection Radio-électrique Batiment de surface Controle) is a fire-control radar developed by France for battleship main guns. Compared to the previously used British radar, this radar has higher accuracy.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_23_desc: Common camouflage is mainly used for disguise and concealment, but the purpose of this camouflage is to cause visual confusion for the enemy, making it difficult to accurately estimate the distance, speed, and course of the ship.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_24_desc: The SP (CXDT) is a lightweight version of the SM Radar. It is used to detect air conditions and provide altitude data, guiding the operation of fighter aircraft. It replaced the SK Radar in the later stages of the war.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_25_desc: The SPS-43 is a two-dimensional long-range air search radar, named "Spring Mattress" due to its shape. This radar has a detection range of up to 500 kilometers and is equipped with an Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) antenna.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_26_desc: The Type 381 three-dimensional air search radar equipped by the Chinese Navy can scan in more directions, providing more accurate data, and plays a crucial role in guiding weapons and air defense.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_27_desc: The Mk-13 Fire-Control Radar is the successor model to the Mk-8, used for main gun fire control. This type of fire-control radar was used until the end of the Cold War.
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_28_desc: The Bulbous Bow is a protruding sphere located below the waterline at the bow of the ship, which can reduce the wave-making resistance of the ship at high speeds. The space in the Bulbous Bow is just right for arranging sonar, and most warships have hydroacoustic equipment arranged inside their Bulbous Bows.

LC_COMMON_weapon_material_10_desc: Top-tier material for manufacturing warship weapons.

LC_COMMON_submarine_explore_desc:
1. Commanders can explore a certain number of times each day. The higher the submarine's level, the more explorations you can conduct daily.
2. There will be different exploration themes each day. Sending officers with corresponding talents during exploration increases the chances of obtaining rare rewards.
3. Enhancing an officer's corps rank and level also increases the probability of obtaining rare rewards!
4. If the number of explorations has not reached the limit, it will automatically be replenished at UTC 00:03.

LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_19_shop_desc:
The main cannon of the Japanese Yamato-class battleship is the largest caliber battleship main cannon in history.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_20_shop_desc:
The Mk 6 cannon demonstrated its formidable power multiple times throughout the history of the United States Navy in World War II.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_21_shop_desc:
The 380 mm/45 Model 1935 cannon is the last type of battleship main gun developed by France, boasting impressive power.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_22_shop_desc:
Made in the Soviet Union, each turret is equipped with a radar rangefinder.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_23_shop_desc:
Lighter than the Mark 9, with stronger firepower.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_24_shop_desc:
Developed based on the old version from WWII, it has seen improvements in both firing rate and anti-aircraft capabilities.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_25_shop_desc:
A product of the Soviet designers' wild experiments, it was never deployed in actual combat. With a total weight of about 10 tons, it could fire shells weighing 250~300 kilograms to a distance of 13,730 meters.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_26_shop_desc:
Made in Germany. The largest caliber naval artillery in history, but it was never used in actual combat.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_27_shop_desc:
The main cannon of the Soviet-class battleship, possessing an ultra-long range and strong penetration power. However, due to the influence of ammunition, it did not achieve the expected effect.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type1_28_shop_desc:
With a total weight of 11.2000 tons, it is the first French triple 152mm turret.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_19_shop_desc:
The Storm Shield variant of the triple-mounted Type 96 25 mm AA gun, equipped exclusively on the Yamato-class battleships. It has a more robust structure and higher strength.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_20_shop_desc:
The automatic rapid-fire cannon for short-range air defense, born in the Soviet Union in the 70s, is highly innovative and advanced.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_21_shop_desc:
Weighing 21 tons, it is equipped with six Bofors guns in pursuit of firepower, and can be linked with the fire control system.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_22_shop_desc:
This type of anti-aircraft gun adopted a layout with independent sights and weapons, and was highly automated, which was a quite advanced design in the 1930s.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_23_shop_desc:
The anti-aircraft gun was developed by the Soviet Union to address its weak air defense issue. In order to enhance performance and power, it used a 45 mm caliber and adopted a chain feed for ammunition, making it an outstanding anti-aircraft gun at the time.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_24_shop_desc:
Utilizes optical tracking/radio command guidance, excels at striking low-altitude sea-skimming aircraft, with high reliability.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_25_shop_desc:
An automatic twin-barrel anti-aircraft gun with radar fire control, with a firing rate of up to 1000 rounds/min.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_26_shop_desc:
The Seaslug is the first generation of anti-aircraft missiles of the Royal Navy of the United Kingdom, with a very unique shape, equipped with four circumferential booster engines at the warhead position.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_27_shop_desc:
The Mk-13 GMLS is a single-arm missile launcher capable of launching various missiles. Due to its unique single-arm design, it is often referred to as the "One-Armed Bandit".

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type2_28_shop_desc:
The OSA-M is a short-range anti-air missile system developed by Russia, used to intercept low-altitude flying targets, and possesses high speed, maneuverability, and infrared guidance capabilities.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_19_shop_desc:
A forward-firing anti-submarine weapon developed by the United Kingdom, based on the principle of a spigot mortar, capable of firing a total of 24 rounds. The name "Hedgehog" comes from its appearance.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_20_shop_desc:
Primarily equipped with the SET-53 series of anti-submarine torpedoes, it can also launch heavy anti-ship torpedoes of the same caliber. Installed on the Type 1135 frigate.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_21_shop_desc:
The Alpha Anti-Submarine Weapon is a type of rocket depth charge launcher. This weapon resembles an artillery piece, but its ammunition is a rocket depth charge (RUR-4).

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_22_shop_desc:
The Limbo Depth Charge Projector, also known as the "A/S Mk.10" Depth Charge Gun, is an improvement from the "Squid" Depth Charge Gun. It has been widely used in the Royal Navy of the United Kingdom, the Australian Navy, and the Canadian Navy.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_23_shop_desc:
The German G7 series torpedoes, the lowercase letters at the end indicate the propulsion method, 'a' for steam, 'e' for electric, and 'u' for hydrogen peroxide. The G7a is used for destroyers and submarines with a caliber of 533mm.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_24_shop_desc:
The Smerch-1 is an anti-submarine equipment from the early Cold War period in the Soviet Union. After learning from the experience of the "Mousetrap", it improved the issues of fixed elevation angle and lack of directional aiming structure.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_25_shop_desc:
The RUR-5 ASROC (Anti-Submarine Rocket) is launched using the MK-112 "Matchbox" Launcher, a type of all-weather, all-sea-state anti-submarine missile system. It is widely used on various warships of the United States Navy.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_26_shop_desc:
Quad-mounted M/50 Anti-Submarine Rocket Launcher, developed by the Swedish Bofors company in 1950. In the 1950s, when the performance of anti-submarine torpedoes was not good, anti-submarine rockets were considered to be good close-range anti-submarine weapons.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_27_shop_desc:
Malafon (MArine LAtécoère FONds) is an anti-submarine missile system developed by France, used for surface vessels to precisely strike and track submarine targets in anti-submarine warfare.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type3_28_shop_desc:
The RPK-3 Metel is a series of Soviet anti-submarine and anti-ship missile systems, developed in the 1960s and deployed on numerous vessels.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_19_shop_desc:
The Mk-8 Fire-Control Radar, composed of 42 rod-shaped antennas, can be used in all weather conditions. It is mainly used for battleships and other large military vessels.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_20_shop_desc:
The Pugliese system, designed by Navy Lieutenant Colonel Umberto Pugliese in early 1917, is a form of "energy-absorbing" protection specifically designed to offset the damage to the underwater hull caused by the explosion of torpedoes or mines.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_21_shop_desc:
This is the fire-control radar for the dual-purpose high-altitude artillery, responsible for directing secondary artillery fire and air defense.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_22_shop_desc:
The DRBC (Détection Radio-électrique Batiment de surface Controle) is a fire-control radar developed by France for battleship main guns. Compared to the previously used British radar, this radar has higher accuracy.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_23_shop_desc:
Common camouflage is mainly used for disguise and concealment, but the purpose of this camouflage is to cause visual confusion for the enemy, making it difficult to accurately estimate the distance, speed, and course of the ship.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_24_shop_desc:
The SP (CXDT) is a lightweight version of the SM Radar. It is used to detect air conditions and provide altitude data, guiding the operation of fighter aircraft. It replaced the SK Radar in the later stages of the war.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_25_shop_desc:
The SPS-43 is a two-dimensional long-range air search radar, named "Spring Mattress" due to its shape. This radar has a detection range of up to 500 kilometers and is equipped with an Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) antenna.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_26_shop_desc:
The Type 381 three-dimensional air search radar equipped by the Chinese Navy can scan in more directions, providing more accurate data, and plays a crucial role in guiding weapons and air defense.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_27_shop_desc:
The Mk-13 Fire-Control Radar is the successor model to the Mk-8, used for main gun fire control. This type of fire-control radar was used until the end of the Cold War.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>
LC_COMMON_weapon_type4_28_shop_desc:
The Bulbous Bow is a protruding sphere located below the waterline at the bow of the ship, which can reduce the wave-making resistance of the ship at high speeds. The space in the Bulbous Bow is just right for arranging sonar, and most warships have hydroacoustic equipment arranged inside their Bulbous Bows.

<COLOR=#8C280A>(Warning: You will receive random attributes when purchasing, but will not gain potential.)</COLOR>

LC_COMMON_t6_res_tile_desc:
Rare Earth Mines produce Rare Earth Metals.

1.You may send troops to gather Rare Earth Metals from any empty tile.
2.The higher the tile's level, the more resources it contains.
3.Guild members receive a 25% boost in gathering speed when gathering on Guild Territory.
4.Resources are transported back to your base when gathering is complete.
5.You may deploy troops to attack a Rare Earth Mine where another player is gathering.

LC_COMMON_t6_in_base_building:
Buildings:

To unlock T6 units, the level cap of buildings in player bases has been raised from Lv. 25 to Lv. 30. The stats of the boosts and base attributes provided by each building have been likewise increased.
LC_COMMON_t6_in_base_lab:
Research:

After the last Zone News ends, a new research category will be unlocked in the Research Lab. Research new technologies to unlock T6 units. The new category also includes technologies to unlock the 6th march queue, increase march, rally, and Garage capacity, increase troop Attack, Defense, Health, and more.
LC_COMMON_t6_out_base_enemy:
Invaders:

The max level of Invaders in players' own Zones has been raised from Lv. 25 to Lv. 50. The initial level of Invaders in the Biozone battlefield has been raised to Lv. 41, and their max level raised to Lv. 70. Their difficulty and rewards are also enhanced accordingly.
LC_COMMON_t6_out_base_iron:
Invaders:

The max level of Steel Behemoths in players' own Zones has been raised from Lv. 5 to Lv. 15. The initial level of Steel Behemoths in the Biozone battlefield has been raised to Lv.16, and their max level raised to Lv. 20. Their difficulty and rewards are also enhanced accordingly.
LC_COMMON_t6_out_base_gather:
Gathering:

Gathering from "Rare Earth Mines" is different from gathering resources like "Food" or "Steel." The map will not generate "Rare Earth Mines" and players must dig from empty tiles to collect this resource. The amount of "Rare Earth Metals" that can be gathered from a tile differs with the level of the tile, but the gathering speed is the same. Gathering speed is affected by gathering boosts. Note: you can be attacked by other players while gathering "Rare Earth Metals."

LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_001_D: Recently, the cold wind has been biting and the drizzle continuous, with very few visitors willing to brave the rain to visit, making the museum appear particularly deserted.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_002_D: Road construction in front of the gate has made passage inconvenient, and the noise has disturbed people. As a result, most tourists abandoned their plans for yesterday.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_003_D: The museum conducted its routine document and artifact inventory, the venue is open but visitors are sparse.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_004_D: The nearby community held a large-scale market event, and most potential visitors chose to attend the market event.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_005_D: A major water pipe has suddenly leaked, and some exhibition areas have to be temporarily closed for emergency repairs.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_006_D: Some employees initiated a strike due to labor disputes, affecting the Museum's normal operations.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_007_D: Due to the city being under attack, a large number of tourists have been evacuated to air-raid shelters.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_008_D: Zombies have been spotted nearby. The Government has issued an emergency warning, and most people have chosen to stay at home.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_009_D: Due to the large-scale battles that occurred in the past few days, the Museum has been temporarily repurposed as a medical rescue station.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_010_D: Due to the fuel shortage caused by the war, heating equipment has stopped working, and the number of tourists has sharply decreased.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_011_D: A serious traffic accident occurred on the main road leading to the Museum, causing a sharp decrease in the number of visitors.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_012_D: A grand Music Festival was held at the nearby square, attracting a large crowd, leaving few visitors inside the hall.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_013_D: The museum conducted a comprehensive staff training, and some exhibition areas are closed.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_014_D: Yesterday experienced a brief power outage, although it was quickly restored, it still affected the visiting experience of some tourists.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_015_D: Despite the holiday, most tourists chose to stay home due to the stormy weather.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_016_D: Some exhibition halls are temporarily closed for renovation, significantly reducing visitors' willingness to visit.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_017_D: A small academic seminar was held inside the Museum, attracting some scholars but not much interest from ordinary visitors.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_018_D: Due to the harsh environment causing a pandemic outbreak, the Government requires reducing crowd gatherings, and the Museum has to limit the number of visitors.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_019_D: The local community gifted us a batch of defense equipment. Visitors can try them on during their visit, but due to the equipment's age, its appeal is limited.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_020_D: The museum has temporarily set up a psychological counseling room to provide mental health support to citizens who have been frightened by the war and zombie attacks.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_021_D: The originally scheduled visits to two schools were canceled for some reason, resulting in a sharp decrease in student traffic.
LC_COMMON_Museum_Event_022_D: An ordinary, unremarkable day with no special events or exhibitions.

LC_COMMON_artifact_material_003_desc: Notes containing some clues about artifacts. Can be used to enhance <COLOR=#69a9ff>Superior</COLOR> Artifacts.
LC_COMMON_artifact_key_silver_desc: Can be opened in the Artifact Market to obtain a Silver Treasure Chest.
LC_COMMON_artifact_key_golden_desc: Can be used to open Gold Treasure Chests in the Artifact Market.
LC_COMMON_museum_rule_content: As our exploration of this world deepens, we have discovered many ancient artifacts. These artifacts emit some mysterious powers that might aid in battles. Artifacts 1. Artifacts can provide us with various powerful boosts. 2. Artifacts or Artifact Fragments can be obtained through the Artifact Market, Excavation, and other means. Collecting a certain amount of Artifact Fragments allows you to obtain artifacts through Repair. 3. Artifacts are classified by quality into Legendary, Epic, and Excellent. 4. Each artifact has Global Buffs and Exhibition Boosts. Exhibition Boosts only take effect when the artifact is displayed in the Exhibition Hall. 5. Enhance artifacts to improve their effects. Artifact Enhancement 1. Use the corresponding Ancient Books and Artifact Fragments to enhance artifacts. 2. The higher the enhancement level, the stronger the boost provided by the artifact. 3. Artifacts can be enhanced up to level 5. Exhibition Hall 1. The Exhibition Hall is used to display artifacts. When artifacts are displayed in the Exhibition Hall, their Exhibition Boosts are activated. 2. At UTC 00:00 daily, the Exhibition Hall will settle the income from the previous day, and the commander can collect the gold coins earned the next day. The amount of gold coins settled daily is related to the rarity of the displayed artifacts and the level of the museum. 3. Unlock more booths by upgrading the museum level. Artifact Market 1. Open treasure chests in the Artifact Market to select various rare artifacts. 2. Silver Treasure Chest: Requires a Silver Key to open, and can be opened once for free daily. 3. Gold Treasure Chest: Requires a Gold Key to open.
LC_COMMON_item_source_artifact_gacha: Can be obtained by opening Treasure Chests in the Artifact Market.
LC_COMMON_item_source_artifact_digging: Gather rare earth metals on empty tiles and complete the collection for a chance to obtain rewards.

LC_COMMON_Artifact_Shard_Name_019: (Fragments) Along the River During the Qingming Festival
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_001: "Venus de Milo" is a marble sculpture created by the ancient Greek sculptor Alexandros around 150 BC. The statue depicts the goddess of love, Venus, with a graceful and elegant figure, plump skin, a beautiful oval face, a Greek-style straight nose, a flat forehead, and a full chin. Her serene expression reflects the intellectual tradition inherited from the peak period of Greek sculptural art.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_002: The Gnoma Lioness originates from the ancient kingdom of Elam in Western Asia, and it was crafted between approximately 3000 BCE and 2800 BCE, during the time when the writing system of Mesopotamia was developing, the wheel was invented, and cities began to emerge. It is considered one of the oldest artifacts from Mesopotamia.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_003: The Magna Carta, also known as the "Great Charter of Liberties," is one of the significant constitutional documents from the feudal period of the United Kingdom. On June 15, 1215, King John of the Plantagenet dynasty was compelled to sign it under the combined pressure of the great feudal lords, clergy, knights, and city citizens. This document limited the king's power under the law and established the principle that private property and personal freedom could not be arbitrarily violated.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_004: The mysterious burial mask of the Mayan Red Queen, made of jade, malachite, obsidian, and limestone. The Maya were typically male-dominated, but the burial artifacts suggest that this was a powerful "queen." Her true identity remains an unsolved mystery to this day.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_005: Dead Sea Scrolls are currently the oldest Hebrew Bible manuscripts (Old Testament). They contain fragments from every book of the Old Testament, as well as an ancient treasure map, which is said to reveal the locations of vast treasures.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_006: The Houmuwu Ding is a casting from the late Shang Dynasty, weighing 832.84 kilograms, making it the heaviest known ancient Chinese bronze artifact. Its discovery proves that the bronze casting in the late Shang Dynasty was not only large in scale but also well-organized and meticulously divided in labor, fully representing the highly developed bronze culture of the Shang Dynasty.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_007: This is a stone sculpture with a diameter of over 1 meter. The radiating pattern resembling a halo and the tongue extending from the skull's mouth are impressive. In Central America, sunset represents death, while sunrise symbolizes rebirth.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_008: Tutankhamun was a pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty during the New Kingdom of ancient Egypt. His life is shrouded in mystery. He ascended to the throne at the age of 9 and died suddenly at 19. There are various speculations about his death—fracture-induced infection, malaria, and even murder. The golden mask found in his tomb is one of the finest art treasures in the world.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_009: The "Mona Lisa" was created between 1502 and 1506 during the peak of the Renaissance. It is an oil painting by the Italian Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci. The painting primarily depicts the typical image of a woman's elegance and tranquility, portraying a woman from the urban bourgeoisie during the rise of capitalism. The profound and noble qualities reflected in the woman in this work mirror the aesthetic ideals and pursuits of beauty for women during the Renaissance.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_010: The Statue of Shiva, King of Dance, is considered one of the most mystically philosophical artworks in India. The bronze statue depicts Shiva dancing the eternal cosmic dance in the earthly cremation ground, symbolizing the processes of creation, preservation, and destruction of the universe. He tramples a demon underfoot, with four dancing and curved arms symbolizing his boundless divine power. He channels his energy into both thought and matter, making them dance in turn, with the flame-like halo representing the universe. The Shiva in the bronze statue has three eyes, signifying his ability to perceive the past, observe the present, and foresee the future.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_011: Bronze artifact from the Eastern Han Dynasty of China, a national treasure-level artifact. The galloping horse is depicted with three legs in the air and one leg surpassing a flying bird. The bird looks back in surprise, further enhancing the sense of the horse's rapid forward motion. The entire force is concentrated on the leg surpassing the bird, accurately grasping the principles of mechanical balance, showcasing an exceptional level of craftsmanship and technical skill.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_012: From the ancient Shu Kingdom over 3000 years ago. The Bronze Statue is the tallest and most complete bronze statue in existence, hailed as the "King of Bronze Statues in the World." Regarding the identity of the bronze figure, some believe it to be a shaman, while others think it is an emperor; there is no definitive conclusion yet.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_013: The Trenholm Sun Chariot, created around the 14th century BCE, is a typical early Nordic Bronze Age artifact. In Norse mythology, Skinfaxi is the horse of the god Dagr. When Dagr drives his chariot across the sky, the earth enters daytime.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_014: Diameter approximately 30 cm, weight 2.2 kg, decorated with blue-green patina and inlaid with gold symbols, which are usually interpreted as the sun or full moon, crescent moon, and stars. This disc is known as the oldest "portable instrument" used for such astronomical measurements.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_015: In 228 BC, the Qin State defeated the Zhao State and obtained the He Shi Bi. Later, the Qin State unified China, and Ying Zheng proclaimed himself the First Emperor. He ordered Li Si to craft the He Shi Bi into the Imperial Seal, which served as the emperor's token. Throughout successive dynasties, the Imperial Seal was always regarded as a symbol of legitimate imperial power. However, in the end, the Imperial Seal was lost during the chaos of war, and its whereabouts remain unknown to this day.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_016: "Stan" is approximately 11 meters long and weighs 7 tons. It is an extremely rare, complete Tyrannosaurus rex fossil. It has 188 original bones, with eyes the size of baseballs. Its teeth are about 28 centimeters long, and it is believed that its bite force is strong enough to crush a car.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_017: The bronze sword from the late Spring and Autumn period was used by King Goujian of Yue. The entire blade underwent vulcanization treatment, greatly enhancing its corrosion resistance and toughness. When unearthed, the sword still gleamed with a cold light and was incredibly sharp, reflecting the advanced sword-making techniques of ancient China. It is considered a rare treasure among ancient weapons.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_018: The cuneiform script on the clay tablet tells a story: a man, following divine instructions, built a boat, brought his family and "all living creatures" aboard, and saved them from an impending flood. This tale bears a striking resemblance to the story of Noah's Ark in the Old Testament of the Bible, but this tablet predates the Bible by about 400 years.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_019: One of the top ten legendary paintings of China, it is the only surviving masterpiece by Northern Song Dynasty painter Zhang Zeduan. The work, in the form of a long scroll, vividly records the urban landscape of Bianjing, the capital of the Northern Song Dynasty, and the living conditions of people from various social classes at that time. It is a testament to the prosperity of Bianjing during the Northern Song Dynasty and a reflection of the urban economy of the Northern Song period. This is unique in the history of painting in China and even the world.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_020: "Code of Hammurabi" is a compilation of laws issued by the ancient Babylonian king Hammurabi around 1776 BC. It is the most representative cuneiform law code and the world's first relatively complete written code of law. The original text is inscribed on a black basalt stele, hence it is also known as the "Stele Law".
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_021: A type of wine vessel popular in the late Shang Dynasty. It weighs 21.4 kilograms and has four elephant-shaped handles on each side, with other unknown animal decorations between the handles. It is one of the important symbols of ancient China's transition from the barbaric era to the civilized era.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_101: In 425 BC, the Athenian navy defeated the Spartan navy at Pylos. This shield was a trophy captured during that battle.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_102: A rectangular monument made of black basalt, with symbols engraved on the top surface, recording Isaac's restoration of Babylon.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_103: Precious relics from ancient Egypt. They showcase the ancient Egyptians' mysterious reverence for life and death.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_104: This pottery piece is finely crafted and beautifully colored, depicting a figure wearing an ornate feathered headdress. The decorations are exquisite and vivid, and the shape is elegant. Such straight-walled pottery might have been used in daily life, or it could have been a vessel for holding holy water in rituals or other activities.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_105: Cloisonné artifacts from the Qing Dynasty of China, these incense burners are typically made of bronze and decorated using the cloisonné technique. Cloisonné is a type of enamel metalwork that uses copper as the base, with the surface inlaid with enamel glaze, and fired at high temperatures to create vibrant colors and intricate patterns.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_106: The Ur Flag is actually a wooden box decorated with intricate mosaic inlays on the exterior. These mosaics use a variety of materials, including lapis lazuli, red marble, and seashells, indicating the extensive trade network of the ancient Sumerians. The size and shape of the Ur Flag are similar to a small suitcase, with a slightly tapered top, giving it a unique appearance.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_107: The Mayan Corn God Statue is a sculpture representing a very important deity in Mayan culture—the Corn God (YumKaax). The Corn God is one of the principal deities in Mayan religion, symbolizing agriculture, fertility, and the regeneration of nature, particularly associated with the growth of corn. Corn is the cornerstone of life and survival in Mayan culture.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_108: Bird-shaped pestles are usually made of wood or stone, with the bird-shaped carvings on top serving both as decoration and possibly holding specific cultural or spiritual significance.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_109: Some jade artifacts from the Timurid period (circa 1370–1507) feature dragon-head decorations on their ends or handles. However, this particular jade piece draws inspiration from Timurid gold prototypes. The cross-guard of this piece adopts the deep green favored by the Timurids, highlighting the stylized ferocity of this mythical beast. The Timurid preference for jade likely stemmed from their belief in its protective properties, a sentiment they also held towards dragons.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_110: During the Fatimid period (969–1171), a significant feature of the artworks produced in Cairo was the notable increase in human and animal motifs, with a high level of craftsmanship. This pendant, crafted with intricate gold and silver filigree on a gold mesh, is an excellent example of fine goldsmithing. The Fatimids borrowed the crescent-shaped ornaments and enamel techniques from Byzantine art, using enamel to decorate the two birds in the center of the pendant.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_111: In ancient Egypt, cattle were not only indispensable animals in agricultural production but also associated with the symbols of several deities. For example, cattle were linked to the goddess of fertility and agricultural abundance, Isis, as well as the sky goddess Hathor. Therefore, these clay bull models might have been used to pray for protection, prosperity, and a bountiful harvest.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_112: Originating from the ancient Minoan civilization on the island of Crete, this was a ritual or sporting event that was very famous in the ancient Mediterranean region. In this event, participants (known as bull leapers or flyers) would attempt to leap over a charging bull in motion. This activity not only showcased physical skill and bravery but also possibly held religious or ritual significance.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_113: Mord Gold Shawl (MoldGoldCape) is an important Bronze Age artifact unearthed in the Mold region of Wales, made around 1900 BC to 1600 BC. This shawl is made of gold, showcasing advanced metalworking techniques and the artistic level of society at that time.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_114: Chloe's Gold (Croeseid) is one of the earliest gold coins in Western history. It is named after King Croesus of Lydia, who ruled Lydia, located in what is now western Türkiye, in the late 6th century BCE. Croesus was one of the first monarchs in history to issue official currency. The issuance of his gold and silver coins marked the beginning of a monetary economy in the Western world.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_115: Discovered in the Lorraine region of northeastern France, near the town of Yutz, these vessels have been called Yutz Wine Jugs. They are made of bronze, with an elegant shape and exquisite decorations. Their size is roughly equivalent to a 1.5-liter wine bottle, with a similar capacity, but they are jug-shaped, featuring handles, lids, and pointed spouts. The shoulders of the jugs are broad, tapering downwards, giving an impression of instability. The first thing that catches the eye about these jugs is the unique decoration on the top, where animals and birds are gathered together.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_116: The Olmec Stone Masks are typically small, intricately carved, and usually made from jade or other types of stone. These masks may represent the faces of deities, ancestors, or important figures, sometimes with exaggerated features and serious expressions. The exact purpose of these masks is not entirely clear, but they may have been used in ritual activities, as decorations, or as burial items for high-status individuals.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_117: This type of lacquerware is characterized by finely detailed autumn grass patterns and the crest of the Toyotomi family. The design of this lacquerware is what later came to be known as the "high-stand style" (referring to black lacquerware adorned with luxurious gold decorations), featuring a striking contrast between two patterns—completely different in color, rhythm, and design. At the time, this style of decoration was not only beloved by lacquerware artists but was also commonly seen in ceramics and brocade.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_118: This exquisite leaf-shaped plate is adorned with embossed floral and bird patterns (using the repoussé technique), making it a quintessential example of Tang Dynasty decorative art.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_119: This pair of silver double-handled goblets represents the pinnacle of ancient Roman metal craftsmanship. The goblets feature high-relief depictions of Cupid, the god of love, either dancing or playing music. The association of Cupid with Bacchanalian revelry makes him a fitting theme for goblets made for lavish banquets, though they may not hold any true symbolic meaning.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_120: The Moche Warrior Terracotta is an important artifact from the ancient Moche civilization, which flourished in what is now northern Peru from around 100 AD to 700 AD. The Moche civilization is renowned for its intricate pottery, spectacular adobe pyramids, and complex social structure.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_121: Lewis Chess Piece共有93件，包括国王、王后、主教、骑士、城堡和兵卒等棋子，每个棋子都有其独特的表情和姿态。这些棋子的设计丰富了中世纪欧洲的文化特色，反映了当时社会的阶层结构和权力象征。
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_122: The design of the Hebrew Astrolabe typically includes several rotatable discs and a fixed base plate. These discs are engraved with constellations, star positions, calendar information, and astronomical data, which can be used to calculate the positions of celestial bodies, time, and other astronomical phenomena. By adjusting these discs, users can simulate the movement of the sky, determine star positions, and perform calendar calculations.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_123: David vs. Bottle was made in 1351, with a height of about 63.6 cm. The bottle is adorned with exquisite blue and white patterns. Detailed inscriptions are engraved on the bottom of the bottle, recording the production time, purpose, and sponsor information. These bottles were originally made for a Taoist temple in Yichun City, Jiangxi Province, and were used for sacrificial ceremonies.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_124: The Holy Thorn Box was specially crafted to preserve and display the Holy Thorns, which are believed to be part of the crown of thorns worn by Jesus during his crucifixion. The design of this box is extremely exquisite, adorned with a large amount of gold and jewels, showcasing the superb craftsmanship of goldsmiths and enamel artists of the time. It is often decorated with intricate religious patterns and symbolic figures, such as angels, saints, and scenes from biblical stories.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_125: In Inca culture, gold is considered the "tears of the sun" and holds strong religious and symbolic significance. Gold is not only used to create decorations for royalty and temples but also for important religious ceremonies and sacrificial activities. Llama statues might be used in sacrificial rituals, symbolizing wealth, prosperity, or sacred offerings.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_126: This golden chariot model not only showcases the craftsmanship of ancient goldsmiths but also reflects the military and ceremonial uses of the time. Chariots were symbols of military power and authority in many ancient civilizations, often used in warfare and royal displays. The use of gold further emphasizes its significant status and ceremonial importance in society.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_127: The Warren Cup was made around the 1st century AD. This cup is crafted from pure silver and is decorated with two detailed relief images on its surface, renowned for its intricate relief decorations.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_128: This beautiful dark blue Venetian glass goblet is adorned with exquisite enamel patterns, making it one of the earliest surviving examples of this decorative technique and scale. The enamel on the goblet evokes illuminated manuscripts and depicts an unreliable story about the Latin poet Virgil, who was imagined as a wizard in medieval folklore. To avenge the rejection of his love by the maiden Phyllis, Virgil used magic to extinguish all the fires in Rome and cruelly demanded that Phyllis expose herself in the marketplace until all the women in the city relit their fires using a burning coal he had placed inside her.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_201: The reverse side depicts a Roman coin featuring the Flavian Amphitheatre. It is said to date back to the early 80s AD.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_202: The Phoenician Silver Coin represents the prosperity of the ancient Phoenicians in the fields of economy, trade, and culture, and also reflects the connections and exchanges between various cultures in the Mediterranean region at that time.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_203: Qin Bronze Crossbow is an important discovery in ancient Chinese military technology, belonging to the Qin Dynasty period (221 BC to 206 BC). This crossbow mechanism is used as the trigger mechanism part of the crossbow (an ancient type of bow weapon), and is usually made of bronze.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_204: The Oduwei Hand Axe is typically oval or pear-shaped, with both sides meticulously polished. The size and shape of these hand axes vary, usually ranging from 12 cm to 20 cm in length. The craftsmanship of these hand axes demonstrates the technological advancements in early human stone tool production. Their symmetry and regular shapes indicate that the makers possessed a high level of skill and aesthetic awareness.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_205: The Clovis spearhead is typically leaf-shaped or oval, characterized by a distinct central groove known as a "flute." This groove extends from the base of the spearhead to the middle or even further, helping to securely attach the stone spearhead to a wooden or bone shaft. This design makes the spearhead more stable during use, capable of withstanding greater impact forces, making it suitable for hunting large animals.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_206: These ornaments hold an extremely important position among ancient gold artifacts in the Mesopotamian region. The pendant represents a deity or a symbol of a deity that can ward off evil and provide protection. People at that time believed that the deities represented by the symbols on the pendants existed in these miraculous forms.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_207: At the end of the 6th century BCE, ancient Greek artists attempted to use various materials to depict the human body in motion. In sculpture, the maturity of bronze casting techniques allowed them to create larger-scale sculptures of moving human figures, far surpassing the scale achievable with stone carvings. In vase painting, the invention of the red-figure technique enabled artists to freely depict decorative images on the surfaces of pottery. On this hard stone, which is less than an inch high, a gem engraver captured the scene of a young man measuring the straightness of an arrow shaft, sculpting his light posture, bulging muscles, and beautiful hairstyle.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_208: This piece of jewelry dates back to 330-300 BC and is a masterpiece of ancient Greek art and craftsmanship. The description of their size and materials showcases the intricacy and luxury of these ornaments.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_209: Since the Classical period, semi-nude statues like this one have been used to depict deities, and commemorative statues of mortals with significant contributions also adopted this form. However, this piece might have originally belonged to a group of sculptures that praised the Julio-Claudian dynasty, which ruled Rome from the time of Augustus until Nero. The stance of this semi-nude statue is reminiscent of the classic works of Polykleitos, the most famous Greek sculptor of the 5th century BCE, almost certainly intended to evoke a heroic atmosphere.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_210: This die-cast bowl is a masterpiece of ancient glassmaking craftsmanship. It is composed of four pieces of translucent glass in purple, yellow, blue, and colorless, all of similar size, and formed in an open mold. Each piece of glass is further adorned with a segment of colored inlaid glass (a cross-section of a bundle of glass rods) to depict a wreath hanging from an opaque white cord. It is known that ancient vessels made from large blocks or strips of glass in different colors are extremely rare, and this bowl is the only known work that combines this technique with inlaid decoration.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_211: This striking ritual vessel is a dual masterpiece of concept and craftsmanship. It is almost certain that it was once a percussion instrument hung up for people to strike. The flanged neck striations resemble the prominent texture of crocodile skin, and they are paired with diamond patterns that may have been used to secure the hanging instrument's ropes. The back of the object is adorned with a human face, spiral bands, and zigzag patterns. This axe can be compared to the "Makassar Axe" housed in the National Museum of Indonesia, which was discovered in southern Sulawesi a century ago.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_212: Throughout the history of Islamic art, inscriptions have played a crucial role in the decoration of objects and buildings. However, on this ceramic bowl from the eastern Islamic world, the use of inscriptions conveys an unparalleled purity and strength. These inscriptions are not only works of calligraphy but also enhance the beauty of the object. This unusually large ceramic bowl is a fine example of such craftsmanship, with inscriptions written in elegant Kufic script: "Prepare for the future and you will have no regrets; Prosperity and peace."
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_213: The inlaid pattern shields of the Solomon Islands are bright and mysterious. Most of them are made by covering a layer of gingerbread wood paste on the surface of a common woven shield, then painting and inlaying mother-of-pearl on it. To date, only about twenty-five such shields remain in the world. These shields always depict a central figure, who might be a warrior or a protective deity, with a horizontal decorative band below, often adorned with human faces, as shown in the shield in the picture. These shields are very fragile and were likely used as ceremonial items to signify social status and valor on the battlefield.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_214: The magnificent painting in the center of the disc and the intricately crafted decorative edges make this piece one of the most important floral ceramics of the fifteenth century.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_215: The Shapur II Silver Plate has a larger diameter and is exquisitely engraved with the image of Shapur II, typically depicting him in hunting scenes or accepting the surrender of enemies. These images not only showcase the king's power and majesty but also reflect the social culture and artistic style of the time.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_216: Oduwei Stone Chopper is typically made from volcanic rock or flint. It is crafted using the percussion flaking technique, where small flakes are struck off from a larger stone to create sharp edges. This simple stone tool is mainly used for cutting, skinning, or chopping, such as processing animal carcasses, cutting plants, or other basic survival activities.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_217: In the late Paleolithic era, reindeer were an important species widely distributed across Europe. For the hunting and gathering communities of that time, reindeer were not only a source of food but also provided materials for making tools and artworks. Carving the image of a mammoth using reindeer antlers might have had specific symbolic meanings, such as worship, commemoration, or a prayer for successful hunting.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_218: The Sumerians were the earliest civilization to use clay tablets for writing, and their writing system was called Cuneiform. This script first appeared around 3200 BCE and was initially used to record trade transactions, taxes, legal, and administrative documents. Over time, the use of Cuneiform gradually expanded to encompass literature, religion, and various scientific fields.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_219: The North American Otter Pipe is carved from stone, finely depicting the image of an otter. This type of pipe is typically associated with the ancient Mound Culture of North America, particularly with the Hopewell Culture in Ohio. The Hopewell Culture is renowned for its exquisite craftsmanship, large mound constructions, and extensive trade networks.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_220: The helmet is exquisitely decorated, featuring intricate metal craftsmanship, including animal-style patterns and symbolic decorations such as masks and animal figures. These decorations not only showcase superb craftsmanship but may also hold symbolic meanings, such as symbols of protection and strength.
LC_COMMON_Artifact_Desc_221: Abd Al-Malik's Gold Dinar is an important currency innovation; it is the first Islamic gold coin purely inscribed in Arabic.

LC_COMMON_KVK_strategy_rule: Fighting in the Biozone requires meticulous strategy and careful progression to defeat the enemy and gain the upper hand. Commanders can now Deploy appropriate Operation Strategies to enhance their combat capabilities. Operation Strategy The Operation Strategy is unlocked in 4 stages, as the Counterattack Progress advances. After each stage is unlocked, the Commander can choose one out of 4 different Operation Strategies to Deploy. *Note: If your base is not in the Biozone, the Operation Strategy will become invalid. Change Strategy After deploying an Operation Strategy, you can change it for 500 Gold. Choose wisely. Unlock Conditions Operation Strategy 1: Unlocked after achieving Event: State Capital I in the Counterattack Progress. Operation Strategy 2: Unlocked after achieving Event: Push Forward in the Counterattack Progress. Operation Strategy 3: Unlocked after achieving Event: Cleansing in the Counterattack Progress. Operation Strategy 4: Unlocked after achieving Event: Investigation in the Counterattack Progress.

LC_EVENT_ExerciseRhine_PreMain_Text1: Take part in the Exercise Rhine, and become the strongest troops in Europe.
LC_EVENT_ExerciseRhine_PreMain_Rule:
1. Before take part in the Exercise Rhine, players can choose difficulty. A higher difficulty will get you better rewards. In each Exercise Rhine, players can only choose difficulty once, and cannot change difficulty during the event.
2. Manoeuvre troops in the Exercise Rhine usually can only be attacked by players themselves or rallied, and other players cannot help. Players can use Help Request Tickets to ask for help. Guild members can help start rally attacks after receiving help requests.
3. After launching a rally attack, you will not be able to receive reinforcements.
4. Help Guild members complete challenges to obtain amazing rewards.
5. You will obtain 5 Help Request Tickets when the Exercise Rhine begins, and you can obtain Help Request Tickets with a certain chance by helping Guild members.
6. When the Exercise Rhine ends, the system will send rewards to you based on the highest level manoeuvre troops you defeated in the event.

LC_EVENT_Monopoly_Rule_Text:
"1. The game board of Sandtable Treasure is comprised of connected steps, players need to advance along the steps to get various rewards. 

2. When the game begins, players start from the starting point and need to spend diamonds to roll the dice to advance. 

3. There are at most 3 types of step on the game board: 
Item step: When reaching this type of step, players get corresponding item rewards! 
Surprise step: There are 3 types of chest on the Surprise step, Bronze chest, Silver Chest and Golden Chest. When reaching a Surprise step the player can open the chest to get rewards!
Critical step: Receive a one-time reward multiplier. The next time you reach a step containing rewards, the rewards will be multiplied by the number you got on the Critical step! 

4. When players reach the terminal, they will get a grand terminal reward and be moved back to the starting point. Afterwards, the rewards on the game board will be reset.

5. When leaving Sandtable Treasure or quitting the game, the game progress will be saved. The progress will be reset only after the activity ends. 

6. Players who advance on the Sandtable Treasure will get points. Also players can test their luck in Try Your Fortune and earn additional ranking rewards!"

1. The Garrison Officer will lead troops to defend against enemies.
2. When the Garrison Officer leaves the city, the Officer remaining with the highest level will automatically become the interim Garrison Officer.
LC_HERO_B2herostory_14:
Cowgirl Lilith comes from the western United States. She used to be the most famous bounty hunter in the Wild Brotherhood, and she gained her excellent shooting and fighting skills from the battles against outlaws.
After the war started, she became an agent of the federal government, fighting enemies on the frontline. Militants are like outlaws, and the cowgirl will uphold the justice with her guns!
LC_HERO_B2herostory_13:
After the country fell, Sister Angel adopted a dozen orphans in a monastery until a missile hit. Angel, who was out looking for food, was the only one who survived the explosion. She loathed the Invaders and swore to drive them out of her homeland.
She then became an underground agent of the federal government, and continued to work as a nun, providing supplies for the government.

LC_HERO_B2herostory_15: Loubna is a mixed-race girl from Morocco who has been training in dancing since childhood and is a well-known dancer in North Africa.But another of her identity is a British spy. Using her advantage well, she managed to make connections with a number of well-known politicians and military officers, thus obtaining a large amount of intel. Of course, commanders should not be blinded by her beautiful clothes. She can also lead an army. It is her strength to confuse and harass the enemy on the battlefield
LC_HERO_B2herostory_16: A fierce figure of German female soldiers, with pure German blood, blonde hair, blue eyes, tall and burly. Cold face, low voice, holding a German standard MP-38.On the battlefield，she is good at using her accumulated Rage to strike the enemy, and shake the enemy's confidence at the same time.
